attributes.context: This sentence follows provisions prohibiting work limitations, quantity restrictions, quotas, and rules or customs that limit production or increase the time required to do work, and it addresses employer-supplied machinery, tools, and labor-saving devices.

extraction_text: There shall be no limitation or restriction of the use of machinery, tools, or other laborsaving devices supplied by the Individual Employer.

attributes.context: The sentence appears in Section XII - Geographic & Market Conditions, where the parties establish a G&M Committee to review and approve changes to the Agreement needed to preserve work opportunities and require the parties to work together on such concerns.

extraction_text: The committee shall meet at least once per quarter and identify and discuss areas of concern to the parties involving issues including, but not limited to non-signatory Employers, private work recovery, new technology, prevailing wages, etc.

attributes.context: The same passage describes a G&M Committee that reviews and may approve changes to the Labor Agreement to preserve work opportunities for covered employees and individual employers, and states that the parties will work together to preserve work opportunities.

extraction_text: The Committee shall meet at least once per quarter and identify and discuss areas of concern to the parties involving issues including, but not limited to, non-signatory Employers, private work recovery, new technology, prevailing wages, etc.

attributes.context: This provision appears in the 2004-2008 Piledrivers Agreement and follows the establishment of a G & M Committee composed of three representatives from the Carpenters conference board and three from the Associated General Contractors Association, which reviews and approves changes to the Labor Agreement to preserve work opportunities for covered employers and employees.

extraction_text: The Committee shall meet at least once per quarter and identify and discuss areas of concern to the parties involving issues including, but not limited to non-signatory Employers, private work recovery, new technology, prevailing wages, etc.
